items.title: Bob Hardaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: And he became a mentor to me and gave me some education and help.

ctx.x: Yeah it’s funny when you think about what your parents do, that sometimes it doesn’t have significance until—

You take it for granted, you know, because I was always exposed to it. Through that I actually met the musical director — he went from there to Walter Lantz, and he was very influential in bringing about Woody Woodpecker as well. And if you think about it © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

they’re pretty much the same characters, they’re both smart alecks. And so I had met the musical director of the cartoons at Walter Lantz, his name was Darrel Calker. And he became a mentor to me and gave me some education and help. I was interested in writing for a while and he was helping me with that. So that was all good. It was all good stuff.
